title: The Enchanted Spring

full_text:
In the mountains of Khorasan lay a legendary enchanted spring known as the Mirror of Souls. Ancient tradition claimed that whoever gazed into its crystal waters would behold not his physical countenance, but the true moral reality of his inner character.

Two travelers journeyed to the spring: the first was a generous young physician named Farhad, who dedicated his life to treating poor shepherds without charge; the second was an envious, grasping merchant named Qasim, who had spent his life cheating widows and short-weighting grain.

Farhad knelt beside the clear pool, cupped his hands, and drank. As he looked into the water, he beheld a vision of a blooming garden filled with singing nightingales, sweet pomegranate blossoms, and crystal streams, feeling an overwhelming peace flood his spirit.

Qasim, eager to see what glory awaited his eyes, pushed Farhad aside and peered into the water.

He shrieked in horror! In the water, he saw not a garden, but a pit of black mud crawling with venomous scorpions, hissing vipers, and thorns, while his own face appeared distorted like that of an ugly goblin!

Qasim fell back onto the grass, trembling: 'The spring is cursed! It is poisoned with witchcraft!'

Farhad offered him a hand and said gently: 'The spring is not poisoned, brother; its water is pure as heaven’s dew. It possesses only one magic: it reflects back to each man the exact garden or swamp he has cultivated inside his own chest. If you wish to see roses in the water, you must first plant seeds of kindness and justice in your life.'

Shaken to his soul, Qasim wept, repented of his greed, returned to his city, and distributed his wealth to the poor, discovering that a purified heart transforms the world into a garden of peace.
moral: A pure heart and good intentions reflect beauty in the world, while malice sees only its own reflection.

quiz.question: What is the central moral lesson taught in "The Enchanted Spring"?
options: Presence of mind and quiet wisdom triumph over brute strength.
Acting in haste and anger without thinking
Believing rumors and flattery without proof
quiz.hint: Remember the moral lesson of this traditional story.

quiz.question: How do the characters overcome their challenge?
options: Through patience, calm reflection, and wisdom
By shouting loudly and blaming others
By running away from every problem
quiz.hint: Consider the virtues praised in world folklore.

quiz.question: What memorable conclusion does this story teach young readers?
options: Honesty, kindness, and clear thinking lead to peace
